body:
Replaces the closed #478 with the simpler approach: cache the binary where the install already happens — no new actions, no workflow changes, no flag plumbing. Measured motivation (lolipopshock/rl-lit run 29309332883, `ubuntu-latest`, warm runtime caches): portal setup = 2.6s runtime restore + **13.1s Claude CLI download**, and every agent-running job pays the download again.

Scope note: this caches the **Claude CLI only**. Codex needs no standalone cache — it arrives via `codex-acp` inside `.agent/node_modules`, which the runtime dependency cache already owns.

## How

Same discipline as the runtime cache, inside the existing install path of `setup-agent-runtime`:

- `Resolve Claude CLI cache key`: env-indirected inputs; `need_claude` short-circuits everything when the CLI is already present (self-hosted). Keys compose the **installer-resolved native platform** (`uname -m` plus musl and Rosetta discriminators — mixed pools can't share incompatible binaries), the **channel** (empty/`latest`/`stable` all rotate on an ISO-week bucket so a mutable channel can't outlive its week; validated pins key exactly), and a reviewed compatibility fingerprint (producer action, adapter lock state, bundled model defaults).
- Best-effort restore (failure ⇒ normal download); the install guard **probes the restored binary by execution** (`--version`), not mere executability, so an incompatible restore falls through to the installer; immediate miss-gated save, never post-job; SHA-pinned `actions/cache` v6.1.0 throughout.

Structural tests pin: env-indirection, single-line output writes, channel case, platform discriminators, key composition, execution probe, need-gated best-effort restore, and save-immediately-after-install ordering.

## Expected effect (hosted runners)

Every Claude-running job — portal, answer, implement, fix-pr, the claude reviewer lane — drops ~11s (13s download → ~1.5–2s restore) after the first weekly warm. Portal setup lands at ~4–6s total; combined with #474's fast-ack, the 👀 target stays ~T+7s. Self-hosted runners with preinstalled CLIs are untouched by construction.

Known trade, on the record: hosted repos ride a CLI up to 7 days old rather than always-latest; pinning `claude_version` restores exact behavior.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #479 replaces closed PR #478’s deferred-install design with CLI caching inside `setup-agent-runtime`. It adds weekly cache keys for unpinned Codex and Claude installations, exact keys for pinned versions, and immediate best-effort saves. The goal is to reduce repeated provider downloads across hosted jobs without changing workflows or self-hosted behavior. The current implementation has one setup-breaking defect, and its new Codex-specific cache cannot execute.

## Review

The design is appropriately scoped, but the current head requires rework. All reviewers confirmed the output-format blocker; current-head inspection also confirms the Codex reachability issue, while reviewers disagreed on whether cache compatibility fingerprints are required.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Invalid multiline output aborts cache-enabled setup | BLOCKING | [`codex_paths`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2505921b27628f8625a9cf203d244eb01557f499/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L219-L225) becomes two physical output-file lines without heredoc syntax. The runner rejects the second line, failing default cache-enabled Codex and Claude setup before restoration or installation. |
| Codex cache is unreachable | WARNING | Runtime dependencies already place the bundled `codex` executable on `PATH` before [`need_codex`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2505921b27628f8625a9cf203d244eb01557f499/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L210-L213) is calculated. Consequently, the new global Codex restore/save path never runs. |
| CLI cache keys lack compatibility fingerprints | WARNING | The keys contain only OS, architecture, and version/week. Runtime, adapter, model-default, or cache-layout changes can therefore continue restoring an incompatible artifact under an unchanged key. |
| cache_mode documentation understates CLI caching | WARNING | The implementation caches CLIs in both `modules` and `full` modes, while the [input contract](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2505921b27628f8625a9cf203d244eb01557f499/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L29-L42) and [documentation](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/2505921b27628f8625a9cf203d244eb01557f499/.agent/docs/usage/internal-actions.md#L7-L10) still describe `modules` as caching only `node_modules`. |

## Progress

- Current head `2505921` has a passing `check` job; reviewer verification also passed 756 runtime, 90 workflow/action, 5 documentation, and 15 shell tests. Those tests are structural and do not exercise the output-file protocol or Codex gate reachability.
- The SHA-pinned cache action, split restore/save design, immediate best-effort saves, and `cache_mode: off` fallback are otherwise well aligned with existing runtime-cache discipline.
- PR #478 was intentionally closed in favor of this simpler approach; PR #474 remains the separate fast-ack component of the broader #454 latency work.
- Posted one distinct [inline comment for the unreachable Codex cache](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/479#discussion_r3590792585). The output blocker was already covered by the existing top-level rubrics review, so it was not duplicated inline; no replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Invalid multiline output aborts cache-enabled setup</summary>

**Cause:** The `$'\n'` expansion writes `codex_paths=…` followed by a bare path. GitHub output files require each value to use `NAME=VALUE` or `NAME<<DELIMITER`.

**Candidate solutions:** Emit package and executable paths as two single-line outputs and combine them under `path: |`, or emit `codex_paths` with proper heredoc syntax. Add a regression assertion covering the output protocol.

**Comments:** All three reviewers agree this is blocking. The green test suite does not execute the generated output file.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Codex cache is unreachable</summary>

**Cause:** `.agent/node_modules/.bin` is added to `PATH` before runtime dependencies are restored or installed. The locked `codex-acp` dependency supplies `@openai/codex`, so `command -v codex` succeeds and `need_codex` remains false.

**Candidate solutions:** Remove the redundant global Codex cache and narrow the feature claims, or define an explicit bundled-versus-global selection contract that makes the cache reachable. Cover the selected behavior with a regression test.

**Comments:** Claude verified that the proposed cached paths are complete but did not account for the earlier gate; Codex identified the reachability issue, and current-head inspection confirms it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CLI cache keys lack compatibility fingerprints</summary>

**Cause:** Neither the producing action nor relevant adapter/model compatibility state participates in the key.

**Candidate solutions:** Add an explicit cache-schema/producer fingerprint plus reviewed compatibility inputs such as the setup action, adapter lock state, and model defaults.

**Comments:** Claude considered OS/architecture/version sufficient because artifacts are upstream-produced and branch-scoped. The other reviewers correctly distinguish cache-poisoning safety from stale runtime compatibility, so the warning remains.

</details>

<details>
<summary>cache_mode documentation understates CLI caching</summary>

**Cause:** CLI restore/save runs for every mode except `off`, but the action input and runtime documentation retain runtime-only descriptions.

**Candidate solutions:** Document that `modules` and `full` enable provider CLI caching, `off` disables it, and unpinned versus pinned installations use weekly versus exact keys.

**Comments:** Reviewers differed between INFO and WARNING severity; this synthesis treats the inaccurate public action contract as required documentation work.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The output protocol and unreachable Codex path require localized branch changes and regression coverage suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items

- [ ] Replace the invalid multiline `codex_paths` output with a supported representation and add output-protocol regression coverage.
- [ ] Remove the unreachable Codex cache or establish an explicit reachable selection/cache contract, with regression coverage.
- [ ] Add reviewed producer and compatibility fingerprints to CLI cache keys.
- [ ] Align the `cache_mode` input and runtime documentation with CLI caching behavior.

**Candidate solutions:** Compute the same native-platform discriminator used by the installer and include it in the key. Add focused glibc, musl, and Rosetta fixtures; optionally probe the restored CLI before skipping installation.

**Comments:** Codex identified this independently, and inspection of the current official installer confirms the platform distinctions. Claude considered the normal hosted-runner path sound, so this primarily protects mixed self-hosted pools.

</details>

**Cause:** The fix round removed the standalone Codex cache without updating the original title and body.

**Candidate solutions:** Describe the change as standalone Claude caching and clarify that Codex remains covered by `.agent/node_modules`.

**Comments:** This is metadata-only and is intentionally excluded from automated branch-change action items.
